newsitem.title: UK: Pearson slips after results hit by charge.
newsitem.headline: Pearson slips after results hit by charge.

text.p: Shares in media and leisure group Pearson Plc were lower in pre-market trade on Monday, after annual operating profits met expectations and the group said it had made a satisfactory start to the year.
The shares were 9p lower at 765p by 0823 GMT.
Pearson announced operating profit of 281 million stg before a 100 million stg charge for improper accounting at its Penguin USA book publishing subsidiary.
Analysts had already been warned of the likely amount of the charge and were predicting pre-exceptional operating profits of between 226-290 million stg.
The annual dividend was raised to 18p per share from 16.5p last year.

Pearson's new chief executive Marjorie Scardino said her immediate priority was to improve the group's financial performance, adding there was considerable scope to increase revenues and reduce costs.
Over the next five years the company also plans to invest up to 100 million stg, extending the Financial Times newspaper and brand internationally.
